dataFlow: When a shopper visits a sold-out product page the storefront widget queries live availability, resolves whether to show a variant-level or product-level signup form, and on submission records a waitlist subscription. When an inventory level update fires, the backend resolves the variant via the inventory item lookup, compares available stock against the last-observed level recorded in item_availability_states, and if the item has transitioned to in-stock it creates a restock_event and enqueues notification_queue rows for the front of the waitlist up to the new stock count (queue-fairness cap). A scheduled job every 5 minutes drains any queued notifications that have passed the quiet-hours window, sending each email with a one-click unsubscribe link. When an order is paid, every line item's variant is checked against the notification_log to attribute a conversion if the shopper was notified about that variant within the prior seven days. The merchant browses the admin dashboard — demand ranking, per-item subscriber drill-in, conversion metrics — all served from pre-aggregated demand_snapshots refreshed on every subscription or notification event.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update delivery for the same item and timestamp — the restock_event unique key on (inventory_item_external_id, inventory_updated_at) makes the insert a no-op and no notifications are double-enqueued.

Partial restock where new stock is fewer units than active subscribers — only the oldest signed_up_at rows up to available_quantity are enqueued; remaining subscribers stay active and are notified on the next restock event.

Stock briefly dips to zero and returns within minutes — the state machine sold-out to in-stock transition creates a new restock_event; the per-restock dedup key (subscription_id, restock_event_id) on notification_queue ensures each subscriber receives at most one email per genuine restock event.

Shopper clicks unsubscribe from an email — the GET /widget/unsubscribe route deactivates all their subscriptions; the queue drain skips any pending notification_queue rows whose linked subscription has is_active set to false.

Product is deleted from Shopify — the products/delete webhook triggers cascade-delete-product-waitlist which sets is_active=false on all subscriptions and cancels pending notification_queue rows for that product before any further emails send.

Back-in-stock email delivery fails permanently — the notification_queue row is marked failed with the reason stored in failure_reason; the subscription remains active so the shopper is eligible for the next restock notification and the failure is visible in the admin drill-in.

Shopper signs up on the widget between the moment inventory drops to zero and the next inventory_levels/update fires — the widget's /widget/availability route calls the Storefront API for live availability so the form is never shown while stock is actually positive; the subscription is valid the moment inventory_levels/update confirms the sold-out state.
